subject: social-studies
title: The Globalisation Supply Chain of One Smartphone
objectives: Explain how a global product crosses borders at every stage
Run the chain in order: Country A mines ($10), Country B makes components ($35), Country C assembles ($70), Singapore sells ($120)
Explain why value rises at every handover along the chain

definitions.meaning: Production and trade spread across countries: for one smartphone, the stages of making it are shared between four countries.
The linked sequence of stages a product passes through, from raw materials to the shop shelf: mine, components, assembly, sale.
The basic materials a product starts from: for the phone, lithium and metals mined in Country A, worth $10.
The working parts made from raw materials: chips, screens and batteries made in Country B, lifting the value to $35.
Putting the components together into a finished product: done in Country C, lifting the value to $70.
The extra worth each stage creates: in the animation it is the bar that rises at every handover - $10, $35, $70, $120.

mechanismSteps: Mine raw materials: value rises to $10 of value - lithium and metals are mined in Country A, the value bar rises to $10 and a route arrow carries the materials on (s1).
Make the components: value rises to $35 of value - factories in Country B turn the materials into chips, screens and batteries, and the value rises (s2).
Assemble the phone: value rises to $70 of value - workers in Country C assemble the components into a finished smartphone, and the value rises again (s3).
Sell it in Singapore: value rises to $120 of value - the finished phone is shipped to a Singapore shop shelf, where transport, branding and retail bring the value to $120 (s4).
workedExample: Work through the whole chain in order. Step 1 (s1): Country A $10 - raw materials are mined and the bar rises to $10. Step 2 (s2): Country B $35 - the materials become components and the bar rises to $35. Step 3 (s3): Country C $70 - the components are assembled into a finished phone and the bar rises to $70. Step 4 (s4): Singapore $120 - the phone is shipped to a Singapore shelf and sold at $120. At every stage the order is the same: Country A $10, Country B $35, Country C $70, Singapore $120, and what links them is the product crossing borders, not one country making everything.

trap.misconception: A global product is made entirely in the country where it is sold, because every stage of making it happens in one place.
trap.explanation: The slip: The finished phone is bought in one shop in one country and carries one brand, so it is easy to assume the whole product was made in that one place. The fix: A global product crosses borders at every stage: raw materials are mined in one country, components are made in a second, the product is assembled in a third, and only then is it shipped to the shop shelf in Singapore - value is added at every handover along the chain. In class, replay scene 1: freeze as the value bar reaches $10 in Country A and ask where the materials go next - then run scenes 2 to 4 and watch each route arrow land as extra value in the next country.
